### `image_krea2_turbo_style_reference`

**Copy the style of a picture** · model: **Krea 2 Turbo — generate in the style of 1–2 pictures** · makes **image**

Upload one or two pictures whose look you like and describe something new: you get your subject made in their style — colours, texture, brushwork — without copying what they show.

> Generate a new picture in the STYLE of one or two pictures you supply. Krea 2 Turbo reads the look — palette, material, light, brushwork, grain — from your references and applies it to whatever you describe, rather than copying their content. One reference is enough. A second is optional and worth adding when the look is more than one thing at once (say a colour palette from one and a material or texture from another) — the references are averaged, so very different pictures give a muddle rather than a blend. The style LoRA was trained on one or two references: the third slot goes beyond that, so expect less from it. Describe the SUBJECT in the prompt and leave the style to the references: "a white yeti with horns reading a book" plus a reference does more than restating the style in words. Style strength controls how hard the reference pulls: 1.0 is the tested setting, lower it towards 0.6 if the subject is being dragged out of shape. Enhance prompt with AI rewrites your sentence into a longer one with a local LLM before generating — useful from a few words, unnecessary when you have already written a full description. It is told to describe only the content and name no style, so the references keep deciding the look.

Prompting: [Krea 2 prompting guide](https://github.com/krea-ai/krea-2/blob/main/docs/prompting.md)
Tip: Describe the subject and the scene; let the reference pictures carry the style. Krea responds well to plain, concrete sentences.

Columns: `prompt` (Prompt — what to draw (the style comes from the references)) · `seed` · `image` Style reference 1 (image, required) · `image2` Style reference 2 — optional (image, optional) · `image3` Style reference 3 — optional, beyond the 1–2 the LoRA was trained on (image, optional)

Settings (a column named by the key; empty keeps the default):
  - `loraloadermodelonly_strength_model_30_15` Style strength (1.0 tested; lower if the subject distorts) — 0…2, step 0.05; default 1
  - `primitiveboolean_value_30_24` Enhance prompt with AI — yes / no; default false
  - `resolutionselector_aspect_ratio_71` Aspect ratio — one of: 1:1 (Square), 2:3 (Portrait Photo), 3:2 (Photo), 3:4 (Portrait Standard), 4:3 (Standard), 9:16 (Portrait Widescreen), 16:9 (Widescreen), 21:9 (Ultrawide); default 1:1 (Square)
  - `resolutionselector_megapixels_71` Size in megapixels (1 = 1024×1024) — 0.25…2, step 0.25; default 1
  - `basicscheduler_steps_30_60` Steps (8 is the Turbo setting) — 4…20, step 1; default 8

### `image_qwen_image_2_1_t2i_fix`

**Crisper close-ups from words, slower** · model: **Qwen Image 2.1 - with the community "Fix" LoRA** · makes **image**

The same picture-from-words model with an add-on that sharpens small things — fingers, watch faces, fine print — in close-up shots. It takes about three times longer and can rearrange wide scenes, so use it for one subject seen up close.

> The same Qwen Image 2.1 text-to-image model as the plain bundle, plus a community adapter that aims to clean up its weak spots - and, just as importantly, the sampling settings its author ships with it. Built to be compared. Run the plain "Qwen Image 2.1" bundle and this one with the SAME prompt and the SAME seed and look at the two side by side. Easier still: set "Fix strength" to 0 here, which keeps every other setting identical and shows you the same seed without the adapter. Two things differ from the plain bundle, and it is worth knowing which is which. The adapter itself changes composition noticeably - it tends toward a glossier, shallower-focus photograph. The settings (guidance raised from 1 to 3, a different sampler, and two model patches) are what sharpen detail and fix muddled small print like a watch dial. On the pictures tested here a good part of the improvement came from the settings rather than the adapter, which is exactly what "Fix strength 0" lets you check for yourself. Guidance above 1 is also why this bundle has a negative prompt at all. At the plain bundle's guidance of 1 a negative prompt does nothing, which is why it does not offer one. It is MUCH slower: about 46 s against the plain bundle's 14 s on this machine, a bit over 3x. That is arithmetic, not a fault - guidance above 1 makes the model run twice per step, and the seeds_2 sampler is a second-order solver that runs it twice again. Same VRAM (about 15 GB), since the adapter merges into the computation rather than sitting in memory. Licence note: Qwen Research License - research and evaluation only, no commercial use.

Prompting: [Qwen-Image-2.1 — official model card](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1) · [Comfy-Org/Qwen-Image-2.1 — the models this bundle runs](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/Qwen-Image-2.1) · [Qwen-Image-2.1-Fix - the adapter and its recommended settings](https://huggingface.co/e-n-v-y/Qwen-Image-2.1-Fix)
Tip: Describe the scene in full sentences and put any words to be rendered in "quotes", saying where they appear.

Columns: `prompt` (Prompt) · `negative` (Negative prompt - what to avoid (only works because guidance is above 1)) · `seed`

Settings (a column named by the key; empty keeps the default):
  - `loraloadermodelonly_strength_model_900` Fix strength - set to 0 to see the same seed without the fix — 0…1.5, step 0.05; default 1
  - `resolutionselector_aspect_ratio_13` Aspect ratio — one of: 1:1 (Square), 2:3 (Portrait Photo), 3:2 (Photo), 3:4 (Portrait Standard), 4:3 (Standard), 9:16 (Portrait Widescreen), 16:9 (Widescreen), 21:9 (Ultrawide); default 1:1 (Square)
  - `resolutionselector_megapixels_13` Size in megapixels (1 = 1024×1024, 4 = native 2K) — 0.25…4, step 0.25; default 1
  - `ksampler_steps_459_458` Steps (20 is the setting this fix was tuned at) — 10…50, step 1; default 20
  - `ksampler_cfg_459_458` Guidance (3 is the tuned setting; the plain bundle is fixed at 1) — 1…6, step 0.5; default 3

### `image_ideogram4_t2i`

**Design a poster with exact words** · model: **Ideogram 4.0 — text to image** · makes **image**

Lay out a poster or graphic in the visual composer: draw a box for each piece of text and each picture, choose your colours, and the words come out spelled exactly. Give every element a box — it also keeps away the false 'blocked' picture.

> Ideogram 4.0 text-to-image. The prompt must be Ideogram's structured JSON "caption": a high_level_description, a style_description, and a compositional_deconstruction listing the background and each element (objects and text, with a box each). Plain text or JSON in another shape usually comes back as a gray "Image blocked by safety filter" picture, even for harmless subjects. Click **Compose visually** under the prompt to build the caption without writing JSON: drag boxes on a canvas shaped like your aspect ratio, describe each element, set the style, the background and colors. The line under the prompt says whether the text is in Ideogram's format. ★ **Give every element a box.** Measured on this rig with one harmless prompt over 5 seeds: no box at all was blocked 5/5, one box on the subject 0/5. Adding boxes for the floor, walls or furniture also fills the scene out. Layout notes, all measured here: boxes are followed closely and placement holds at every aspect ratio and size. Draw each box the shape the thing should be — a tall narrow box makes text read vertically (sometimes upside down). Boxes left apart in empty corners can make Ideogram split the frame into separate panels; keep them adjacent or add floor/wall boxes to hold one scene. In tall formats (9:16, 3:4) elements drift a little towards the middle. Output sizes: 1 MP gives 1024×1024 (1:1), 1376×768 (16:9), 768×1376 (9:16), 896×1184 (3:4), 1568×672 (21:9); 0.25 MP and 2 MP scale that (688×384 and 1936×1088 at 16:9). Quality presets: Turbo (12 steps, fast) / Default (20) / Quality (48, slow & best).

Prompting: [Ideogram 4.0 JSON prompting guide — Ideogram](https://docs.ideogram.ai/prompting/json-prompting) · [Ideogram 4 open-weights prompting notes](https://github.com/ideogram-oss/ideogram4/blob/main/docs/prompting.md)
Tip: Fill the JSON: a high_level_description, an optional style_description and a compositional_deconstruction listing every object and text element (the words to render go in their own text element); colors as #RRGGBB.

Columns: `prompt` (Prompt (structured JSON)) · `seed`

Settings (a column named by the key; empty keeps the default):
  - `aspect_ratio_37` Aspect ratio — one of: 1:1 (Square), 2:3 (Portrait Photo), 3:2 (Photo), 3:4 (Portrait Standard), 4:3 (Standard), 9:16 (Portrait Widescreen), 16:9 (Widescreen), 21:9 (Ultrawide); default 9:16 (Portrait Widescreen)
  - `megapixels_37` Megapixels — 0.25…2, step 0.25; default 1
  - `quality_98_156` Quality preset — one of: Turbo, Default, Quality; default Default
  - `cfg_98_155` Guidance (CFG) — 1…20, step 0.5; default 7

### `image_qwen_image_2_1_t2i`

**Draw busy scenes exactly as described** · model: **Qwen Image 2.1 — text to image** · makes **image**

Describe a scene in full sentences — where each thing sits and what every label or sign says — and it draws all of it, up to large 2K prints. Pick it when a picture has many parts or small writing; it can also make cut-outs with a see-through background.

> Make an image from a written description with Qwen Image 2.1. It is unusually good at TEXT inside the picture — signs, posters, packaging, handwriting — so put the words you want rendered in quotes and say where they sit. Size: the default 1 megapixel is 1024×1024. This model is trained for 2K, so for a big print set the size to 4 megapixels (2048×2048 at 1:1). Pick the aspect ratio first; the width and height follow. Transparent PNG: wrap your prompt exactly like this (the wording Qwen's model card gives) and the model returns a cut-out with a real alpha channel — "This is an RGBA image with transparency. <your subject>. The image has alpha channel and the background is transparent." Steps: 25 is a quick pass. Qwen's own pipeline uses 40–50, which is worth it for detailed scenes and for clean lettering. There is no negative prompt: guidance is fixed at 1, which is how this model is meant to run.

Prompting: [Qwen-Image-2.1 — official model card](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1) · [Comfy-Org/Qwen-Image-2.1 — the models this bundle runs](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/Qwen-Image-2.1)
Tip: Describe the scene in full sentences and put any words to be rendered in "quotes", saying where they appear. For a transparent PNG, use the RGBA wording in the description above — it is the phrasing Qwen's model card gives.

Columns: `prompt` (Prompt) · `seed`

Settings (a column named by the key; empty keeps the default):
  - `resolutionselector_aspect_ratio_13` Aspect ratio — one of: 1:1 (Square), 2:3 (Portrait Photo), 3:2 (Photo), 3:4 (Portrait Standard), 4:3 (Standard), 9:16 (Portrait Widescreen), 16:9 (Widescreen), 21:9 (Ultrawide); default 1:1 (Square)
  - `resolutionselector_megapixels_13` Size in megapixels (1 = 1024×1024, 4 = native 2K) — 0.25…4, step 0.25; default 1
  - `ksampler_steps_459_458` Steps (25 is quick, 40–50 is Qwen's own setting) — 10…60, step 1; default 25

### `image_qwen_image_2512_360_panorama`

**Make a 360° look-around panorama** · model: **Qwen-Image 2512 — 360° panorama / HDRI from a description** · makes **image** · experimental

Describe a place and pick the time of day, season, sky and camera height; you get a full 360° picture to look around in the viewer, or to use as the sky and lighting of a 3D scene in Blender, Unity or Unreal.

> A 360° panorama of a place you describe, generated with Qwen-Image 2512 and the qwen-360-diffusion LoRA — usable as an HDRI/skybox in Blender, Unreal, Unity or a VR viewer. Describe only the PLACE and the camera ("a quiet mountain pasture above an alpine village … sharp realistic photograph"). Time of day, season, sky and camera height are chosen from the lists and added to your words for you, together with the 360° instructions, so leave lighting and weather out of the prompt. You get a 4096×2048 equirectangular picture as a 16-bit PNG, plus a 32-bit float EXR under the download buttons. Open the picture and press **View in 360°** to look around inside it. ★ The EXR is the same picture stored as linear float, not a true high-dynamic-range capture: the sun is not brighter than white, so it lights a 3D scene evenly rather than with hard sun shadows. The seam repair re-paints a band across the left/right join so the panorama wraps without a visible line. Outdoor scenes work best; the poles (straight up and down) can stay soft. Quality mode drops the 8-step Lightning LoRA for a slower 30-step render.

Prompting: [qwen-360-diffusion — model card (trigger words, 2:1 sizes)](https://huggingface.co/ProGamerGov/qwen-360-diffusion)
Tip: Name the place and the medium ("photograph of …"); the 360° trigger and the horizon instructions are added for you.

Columns: `prompt` (The place — what surrounds the camera (and the camera, e.g. “sharp realistic photograph”)) · `negative` (Negative prompt (only used in quality mode)) · `seed`

Settings (a column named by the key; empty keeps the default):
  - `time_of_day_3` Time of day — one of: 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7; default 4
  - `season_4` Season — one of: 0, 1, 2, 3; default 1
  - `clouds_5` Sky (the exact clouds follow the season) — one of: 0, 1, 2, 3, 4; default 1
  - `camera_height_6` Camera height — one of: 0, 1, 2; default 0
  - `seam_fix_9` Repair the left/right seam (a second pass over the join) — yes / no; default true
  - `seam_denoise_10` Seam repair strength (0.5–0.7) — 0.3…0.9, step 0.05; default 0.6
  - `quality_mode_11` Quality mode — no Lightning LoRA, several times slower — yes / no; default false
  - `steps_8` Steps in fast mode (8 recommended, 6–10) — 4…12, step 1; default 8
  - `quality_steps_12` Steps in quality mode (25–40) — 20…50, step 1; default 30
  - `quality_cfg_13` Guidance in quality mode (CFG 2.5–4) — 1.5…5, step 0.5; default 3

### `image_minimax_h3_t2i`

**Make a cinematic film still** · model: **MiniMax H3 — text to image** · makes **image** · experimental

Describe a shot like a film director — lens, light, movement, weather — and get a single frame from a model trained on films: strong at motion blur, rain, flares and mood. It needs the whole graphics card, so it is slow to start.

> A still picture from MiniMax H3 — the video-and-sound model, asked for a single frame. Because it was trained on film, it is strong at cinematic framing, light and atmosphere: write the picture the way a director of photography would describe a shot — subject, setting, lens and angle, light, colour palette, medium. Fast mode (on) uses the 8-step turbo LoRA. Turn it off for the base model at the steps below (30 by default, up to 50 for the most detail) — about four times slower. It loads a 20 GB model plus a 15 GB text encoder, so the first picture after a model change takes a while; it owns the card on a 32 GB GPU.

Prompting: [MiniMax H3 — official prompt guide](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3/blob/main/docs/VIDEO_PROMPT_WRITING_GUIDE_base_en.md)
Tip: Describe it like a film frame: subject, setting, lens and angle, light and palette. H3 keeps improving with more steps.

Columns: `prompt` (Prompt) · `seed`

Settings (a column named by the key; empty keeps the default):
  - `fast_mode_200` Fast mode — 8-step turbo LoRA (off: base model, slower, a little more detail) — yes / no; default true
  - `aspect_ratio_79` Aspect ratio — one of: 1:1 (Square), 2:3 (Portrait Photo), 3:2 (Photo), 3:4 (Portrait Standard), 4:3 (Standard), 9:16 (Portrait Widescreen), 16:9 (Widescreen), 21:9 (Ultrawide); default 16:9 (Widescreen)
  - `megapixels_79` Size in megapixels (1.0 ≈ 1344×768 at 16:9) — 0.25…2, step 0.05; default 1

### `image_minimax_h3_image_t2i`

**Make a very large, detailed picture** · model: **MiniMax-H3-Image — text to image** · makes **image** · experimental

Describe a picture in detail and get it back large and finely drawn: posters, packaging, photos, diagrams with readable text.

> Generate an image from a text prompt with MiniMax-H3-Image, an open-weights image model whose single checkpoint handles both text-to-image and editing. Generation is distilled to 6 steps with no CFG. It does not work well at low resolution: it is made for about 4 to 20 megapixels and is at its best near 16 MP. At the default 4 MP (2048x2048) a picture takes about 16 seconds once the models are loaded; 16 MP (4096x4096) took 46 seconds, visibly finer, but fills the whole 32 GB graphics card. Describe the whole picture in detail, in English (subject, setting, light, materials, any words to be written in quotes), and write what to avoid into the prompt too: there is no negative prompt. The prompt improver writes such a description from a short request; it is off by default and adds about a minute. It may add things the prompt does not ask for. Not the same model as the 'MiniMax H3 — text to image' card, which runs the H3 video model on a single frame. Experimental.

Prompting: [MiniMax-H3-Image — model card (MiniMax)](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3-Image) · [MiniMax-H3-Image in ComfyUI (Comfy docs)](https://docs.comfy.org/tutorials/image/minimax/minimax-h3-image)
Tip: Describe the whole picture in English, in detail. There is no negative prompt: write what to avoid into the prompt too. Your pictures are <Picture 1>, <Picture 2>… in upload order.

### `image_krea2_turbo_t2i_lora`

**Pick a style, make a picture** · model: **Krea-2 Turbo — text to image (+ style LoRA)** · makes **image**

Pick a ready-made look from the list — embroidery, ink wash, retro anime, watercolour, tarot card… — and describe your scene; the card adds the words that switch the style on.

> Fast text-to-image with Krea 2 Turbo (8 steps). Type a prompt, pick an aspect ratio and, if you like, a style LoRA. "Enhance prompt with AI" lets a small language model rewrite your prompt into a richer description before the image is made; untick it to use your words exactly as written. Keep "Thinking mode" on: with it off, the rewrite sometimes comes back as the AI's working notes, an empty answer or a refusal instead of a description (when ComfyQ can tell, it uses your own words instead). "Use a style LoRA" applies a trained look (realism is the default). Each style's trigger words are added to the prompt automatically, and while a style LoRA is on the AI rewrite leaves style words out so the LoRA's look is not mixed with another one. Around 1.0 is a good strength; some styles look best near 0.8.

Prompting: [Krea 2 prompting guidelines — Krea](https://github.com/krea-ai/krea-2/blob/main/docs/prompting.md) · [Krea 2: start vague, then refine — Krea blog](https://www.krea.ai/blog/explorative-prompting-krea-2)

### `image_moss_image_base_t2i`

**Place characters with boxes** · model: **MOSS-Image Base — text to image, with an optional box layout** · makes **image** · experimental

The same box-layout picture maker in its raw, untuned form: draw where each character, object and caption goes and describe the whole picture. For neater text pick the other box-layout card, "Place text and objects with boxes" (MOSS-Image SFT); this one is the version style add-ons are made for.

> MOSS-Image, a 5B text-to-image model with strong text rendering and layout control, running the BASE checkpoint — no post-training, so it groups text less neatly than the SFT box-layout card (on the same layout it followed the boxes as well, a little flatter), and it is the one community LoRAs are trained on. Write a long, concrete caption rather than a few keywords — the model was trained on 200–500 word descriptions. Open with the medium and subject ("Studio photograph of …", "Grunge event poster: …"), then pose, setting, framing, light and tone. Put every word that must appear in the picture in double quotes; use a real line break where the text should break. ★ Layout (optional): press **Compose layout** under the Layout field to draw boxes on a canvas shaped like your aspect ratio. Each box is an object or a piece of text with its own description; tick “Character” on a box that holds a person or creature. Add the background first and the foreground last. Left empty, the prompt is used on its own. Layout control is experimental in MOSS-Image itself. “Improve my prompt with AI” rewrites the overall caption with the model's own text encoder (the boxes are left untouched). It adds about a minute and a half; or write the full caption yourself. Settings: 25 steps / CFG 2.5 is a fast setting; the official one is 50 steps / CFG 3. Skip-layer guidance sharpens detail but can over-bake anime styles. Best sizes are 1, 1.5 or 2 megapixels.

  - `aspect_ratio_19` Aspect ratio — one of: 1:1 (Square), 2:3 (Portrait Photo), 3:2 (Photo), 3:4 (Portrait Standard), 4:3 (Standard), 9:16 (Portrait Widescreen), 16:9 (Widescreen), 21:9 (Ultrawide); default 1:1 (Square)

  - `cfg_107` Guidance (CFG — 2.5 fast · 3 official) — 1…6, step 0.5; default 2.5

### `image_qwen_image_2_1_control_depth`

**Re-imagine a photo, keeping its space** · model: **Qwen Image 2.1 - draw from depth (ControlNet depth)** · makes **image**

Upload a photo — of a scale model, a room, a landscape — and describe a new picture; what is near and far and the shape of everything stays, while your words decide what it all is. Better than the outline version for soft photos and real places.

> Upload a picture and the model draws something NEW that keeps its SHAPE and depth - what is near, what is far, how the space is arranged - while the prompt decides what everything actually is. Depth holds on to volume and composition rather than outlines, so it copes with soft or busy photographs where edge control struggles, and it is the better choice for landscapes, portraits and anything where the silhouette matters more than the fine lines. A depth map is worked out from your picture automatically - you upload an ordinary photograph. If the result follows the original too literally, lower the control strength. The structure picture is scaled to the output size you choose, so pick an aspect ratio close to it or it will be cropped to fit. ### `image_moss_image_color_depth_control`

**Reinvent a photo, keep its pose** · model: **MOSS-Image — new picture from a photo's pose and depth** · makes **image** · experimental

Upload a photo of someone (or something) and describe a completely new picture; only the pose and framing come from the photo — the person, clothes, place and style all come from your words.

> Drop in a photo and get a NEW picture with the same pose and framing. The photo's 3D shape is estimated (MoGe 3) and turned into a depth map; MOSS-Image then paints whatever the prompt says onto that shape. Nothing else of the photo is kept — identity, clothes, material, light and style all come from the text. Describe the whole picture as if from scratch, including the parts the photo already shows ("a woman framed from the chest up…"). If the photo has a feature the shape will keep — pointed ears, a hat — either describe it or say how to hide it. Geometry: "depth" holds the pose, the face profile and the background falloff; "mask" keeps only the silhouette and leaves the prompt more room. Control ends at 60% of the steps by default so the last steps can render freely — raise it to pin the shape harder. The output takes the photo's shape, at about 1 megapixel.

Prompting: [MOSS-Image — official user guide](https://github.com/OpenMOSS/MOSS-Image/blob/main/USERGUIDE.md) · [MOSS-Image colour/depth control adapter](https://huggingface.co/darask0/MOSS-Image-color-depth-control)
Tip: Describe the whole picture from scratch: subject, clothes, material, setting, framing, light and style. The photo only gives the shape.

Settings (a column named by the key; empty keeps the default):
  - `geometry_175` Geometry taken from the photo — one of: depth, mask; default depth
  - `strength_53` Control strength (1.0 is what the adapter was trained at) — 0…2, step 0.05; default 1
  - `end_percent_53` Control ends at (fraction of the steps — 1.0 pins the shape to the end) — 0.1…1, step 0.05; default 0.6
  - `megapixels_77` Size in megapixels (the photo's shape is kept) — 0.25…2, step 0.05; default 1
  - `steps_22` Steps — 10…50, step 1; default 25
  - `cfg_20` CFG — 1…8, step 0.5; default 3

### `image_qwen_image_2_1_control_canny`

**Turn a drawing into a photo** · model: **Qwen Image 2.1 - draw from edges (ControlNet canny)** · makes **image**

Give it a drawing, a line sketch or a photo with clear outlines and describe what it should become; every line stays exactly where it was drawn and everything else comes from your words. Best for drawings, buildings and objects with crisp edges.

> Upload a picture and the model draws something NEW that keeps its outlines - the shapes and the layout stay, everything else comes from your prompt. It works from the edges of your picture, so it is at its best where structure is made of clear lines: buildings, objects, vehicles, interiors, a strong silhouette. A hazy or very soft photograph gives it little to hold on to. Two edge controls decide how much of the picture it traces. Lower "edge detail" finds more lines, including texture you may not want; raise "edge strength" to keep only the confident ones. If the result feels like a tracing, lower the control strength. The structure picture is scaled to the output size you choose, so pick an aspect ratio close to it or it will be cropped to fit. Licence note: the ControlNet weights are Qwen Research License - research and evaluation only, no commercial use.

Prompting: [Qwen-Image-2.1 — official model card](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1) · [Comfy-Org/Qwen-Image-2.1 — the models this bundle runs](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/Qwen-Image-2.1) · [Qwen-Image-2.1-Fun-Controlnet-Union - the control model](https://huggingface.co/alibaba-pai/Qwen-Image-2.1-Fun-Controlnet-Union)
Tip: Describe the scene in full sentences and put any words to be rendered in "quotes", saying where they appear.

Settings (a column named by the key; empty keeps the default):

  - `canny_high_threshold_901` Edge strength - higher keeps only strong lines — 0.01…0.99, step 0.01; default 0.8

  - `resolutionselector_megapixels_13` Size in megapixels (1 = 1024×1024, 4 = native 2K) — 0.25…4, step 0.25; default 1
  - `ksampler_steps_459_458` Steps (20 is the default, 25 is quick, 40–50 is Qwen's own setting — slower) — 10…50, step 1; default 20

## Editing a video (`video-edit`, 16)

### `video_edit_bernini_r_video_editing`

**Change one thing in a video** · model: **Wan 2.2 Bernini-R — AI video editing** · makes **video**

Upload a short clip and say in words what to change — a colour, an object, the sky — and the clip comes back with only that changed, the people, their moves and the scene left as they were. Keep clips to a few seconds; it takes several minutes.

> Edit or restyle a short video by describing the change in words. Upload a clip and type an instruction — the Bernini-R model (Wan 2.2) regenerates the clip following your prompt while keeping its motion and timing. The original audio is carried through. • Pick an **edit type** to steer the model (Style / Motion, Action / Position, Content Propagation, or general Video Editing). • **Fast mode** (Turbo LoRA) is on by default — ~6 steps, quick and light. Turn it off for slower, higher-quality 40-step runs. • Only the first few seconds are processed (set the clip length) — keep clips short, video editing is heavy. * Use small resolutions then upscale : 480 x 832 px in portrait and 832x480 px in landscape. For editing guided by a reference image, use the "with reference" version instead.

Prompting: [Bernini — official example edits](https://github.com/bytedance/Bernini/tree/main/assets/testcases)
Tip: One clear instruction: say what changes and what must stay the same. Match the clip's shape — the video is centre-cropped to width × height.

Columns: `prompt` (Edit instruction) · `seed` · `video` Source video (video, required)

Settings (a column named by the key; empty keeps the default):
  - `customcombo_choice_76_54` Edit type — one of: Video Editing, Video Editing (Content Propagation), Video Editing (Action / Position), Video Editing (Style / Motion); default Video Editing
  - `primitiveboolean_value_76_70` Fast mode (Turbo LoRA — faster, lower quality) — yes / no; default true
  - `video_slice_duration_109` Clip length (seconds) — 1…10, step 1; default 5
  - `berniniconditioning_width_76_50` Width (Bernini Conditioning); default 832
  - `berniniconditioning_height_76_50` Height (Bernini Conditioning); default 480

### `video_edit_bernini_r_video_editing_with_reference`

**Copy an outfit onto a video** · model: **Wan 2.2 Bernini-R — video editing with a reference image** · makes **video**

Give it a clip of a person and a photo of clothes — worn by someone or on a hanger — and the person in the clip comes back wearing them, with the same face, moves and scene. Takes several minutes; keep clips short.

> Put the clothes from a photo onto the person in a short video. Upload a clip, a reference photo of an outfit and an instruction — the Bernini-R model (Wan 2.2) regenerates the clip so the person wears that outfit, keeping their face, the scene, the motion and the timing. A photo of the clothes worn by someone works better than clothes laid flat. The original audio is carried through. Write the instruction as the swap plus what must stay, like the default: "Replace the person's clothing with the outfit from the reference image. Keep the face, hair, background, lighting, camera and all motion unchanged." Describing the new outfit and the result helps. This card is for outfit and look swaps, not for copying the general style of a picture: in one test, asking it to match the look of a poster changed only the sky. • **Edit type**: keep "Video Editing with Reference". "Ads / Content Insertion" here only changes the model's first instruction line: Bernini's real ad-insertion task takes a second video, which this card has no slot for. • **Fast mode** (Turbo LoRA) is on by default — ~6 steps. Turn it off for slower, higher-quality 40-step runs. • Only the first few seconds are processed (set the clip length) — keep clips short, video editing is heavy. For editing by text alone (no reference image), use the plain video-editing version instead.

Prompting: [Bernini — official example edits](https://github.com/bytedance/Bernini/tree/main/assets/testcases)
Tip: One clear instruction: say what changes and what must stay the same. Match the clip's shape — the video is centre-cropped to width × height.

  - `customcombo_choice_76_54` Edit type — one of: Video Editing with Reference, Ads / Content Insertion; default Video Editing with Reference
  - `video_slice_duration_109` Clip length (seconds) — 1…10, step 1; default 5

### `video_edit_minimax_h3_fun_controlnet_union`

**Copy someone's moves onto anyone** · model: **MiniMax H3 ControlNet (pose) — transfer a person's movement + audio** · makes **video**

Upload a video of a person moving and describe who should move like that, and where; you get a new character doing exactly the same moves, with new sound.

> Upload a video of someone moving (a dance, gestures, a sports move) and describe who should perform it and where. The people in the clip are detected and a full-body skeleton (body, hands, face, feet) is tracked on every frame; MiniMax H3 then generates a brand-new video where your described character performs exactly those movements, with a matching audio track. Clothing, face, background and lighting all come from your prompt. The people must be clearly visible — ideally the whole body, not too small in the frame. Without a detectable person the pose is guessed and the movement is not followed. "Max people to track" sets how many dancers are followed; "Control strength" sets how strictly the pose is copied (1 = exactly, lower = looser). Only the first seconds of your clip are used ("Duration", default 5 s), and the video is centre-cropped to the aspect ratio you pick. The result is always 24 frames a second and follows your clip frame by frame, so a 30 fps clip (what most phones record) comes out about 25% slower: export it at 24 fps first if the timing matters. Pose tracking adds a little time on top of the render; "Fast mode" (4-step turbo LoRA) is several times faster at some cost in quality.

Prompting: [MiniMax H3 Fun-ControlNet in ComfyUI](https://docs.comfy.org/tutorials/video/minimax/minimax-h3-fun-controlnet) · [MiniMax H3 prompt guide (ComfyUI) — what works and what does not](https://docs.comfy.org/tutorials/video/minimax/minimax-h3-prompt-guide) · [MiniMax H3 reference-mode prompt guide — MiniMax](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3/blob/main/docs/VIDEO_PROMPT_WRITING_GUIDE_ref_en.md)

Columns: `prompt` (Prompt (new character / scene / camera / sound)) · `seed` · `video` Source video (a person moving - dance, gestures, sport) (video, required)

Settings (a column named by the key; empty keeps the default):
  - `primitiveboolean_value_146` Fast mode (4-step turbo LoRA) — yes / no; default false
  - `resolutionselector_aspect_ratio_115` Aspect ratio (pick the one closest to your video) — one of: 1:1 (Square), 2:3 (Portrait Photo), 3:2 (Photo), 3:4 (Portrait Standard), 4:3 (Standard), 9:16 (Portrait Widescreen), 16:9 (Widescreen), 21:9 (Ultrawide); default 16:9 (Widescreen)
  - `resolutionselector_megapixels_115` Size in megapixels (0.4 = 864x480 at 16:9, 1.0 = 1376x768) — 0.2…1, step 0.1; default 0.4
  - `primitivefloat_value_132` Duration (seconds, 2-15) — 2…15, step 1; default 5
  - `minimaxh3funcontrolnetapply_strength_172` Control strength (1 = follow the video closely, lower = looser) — 0…2, step 0.05; default 1
  - `rtdetr_detect_max_detections_700_678` Max people to track — 1…5, step 1; default 2

### `video_edit_minimax_h3_v2v_video_reference`

**Edit a video, sound and all** · model: **MiniMax H3 — transform a video by reference + audio** · makes **video**

Upload a clip and say what to swap — the person, a costume, an object, the setting — and what to keep; you get the same shot, the same moves and timing, with your change and a new soundtrack. Slow (several minutes).

> Upload a source clip and describe how to transform it. MiniMax H3 watches your clip as a reference (call it <Video 1> in the prompt, with the angle brackets) and generates a new video that keeps what you ask it to keep — choreography, timing, camera move — and replaces what you name: a person, a costume, an object, the setting. It is an EDIT of your clip; to restyle the whole clip (everything in clay, in watercolour...), the canny and depth cards do that better. A new audio track is generated from your prompt. Nothing is traced frame by frame (unlike the ControlNet versions), so the wording matters a lot: say explicitly what to retain from <Video 1> and what to change. Write it the way the model was trained, as the default prompt does: name the clip <Video 1> with the angle brackets, start the summary with [video editing] and "The target video is an edited version of <Video 1>.", mark each element removed, partially_preserved or attribute_transfer under retention_analysis, then the shot, and the sound under overall_soundscape and non_diegetic_music. A prompt that names "Video 1" without brackets, or asks to keep everything, gets the source back unchanged. This is the slowest MiniMax workflow: the whole reference clip rides along every sampling step. Keep clips short ("Duration", default 5 s; only the start of your clip is used) and use "Fast mode" (4-step turbo LoRA) when you are exploring ideas.

Prompting: [MiniMax H3 reference-mode prompt guide — MiniMax](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3/blob/main/docs/VIDEO_PROMPT_WRITING_GUIDE_ref_en.md) · [H3 prompt tips for ComfyUI — Comfy-Org](https://docs.comfy.org/tutorials/video/minimax/minimax-h3-prompt-guide)
Tip: Say what to keep from each input and what changes; describe the action, camera and sound concretely — everything should be visible or audible.

Columns: `prompt` (Prompt (what to keep from Video 1, what to change, sound)) · `seed` · `video` Source video (Video 1 - the clip to transform) (video, required)

Settings (a column named by the key; empty keeps the default):
  - `primitiveboolean_value_146` Fast mode (4-step turbo LoRA) — yes / no; default false
  - `resolutionselector_aspect_ratio_115` Aspect ratio of the result — one of: 1:1 (Square), 2:3 (Portrait Photo), 3:2 (Photo), 3:4 (Portrait Standard), 4:3 (Standard), 9:16 (Portrait Widescreen), 16:9 (Widescreen), 21:9 (Ultrawide); default 16:9 (Widescreen)
  - `resolutionselector_megapixels_115` Size in megapixels (0.4 = 864x480 at 16:9, 1.0 = 1376x768) — 0.2…1, step 0.1; default 0.4
  - `primitivefloat_value_132` Duration (seconds, 2-10) — 2…10, step 1; default 5

### `video_edit_wan_animate2`

**Give a character a video's moves** · model: **Wan Animate 2 — make a character perform a video's motion** · makes **video**

Upload a full-body picture of a character and a video of someone moving; your character performs the same moves in the setting of your picture — the prompt adds details to that place but does not replace it. For a place described in words, use the "Keep the moves, change everything else" card (LTX 2.5 IC-LoRA, pose control) instead.

> Give your character someone else's moves. Upload a picture of your character (who) and a driving video of a person moving (what motion) — Wan Animate 2 makes your character perform that motion. The motion is read straight from the video frames; no skeleton or pose extraction is needed. There are two prompts. The Character & scene prompt describes how the character looks and details of the scene — looks only, no motion words. ComfyUI says the background comes from this text alone, but in both tests on this machine it came from the picture: a full-frame photo kept its own concrete plaza (the prompt's beach only added palm trees to it), and a picture of the character on a plain grey background kept a plain studio background instead of the prompt's cliff top. So expect your picture's setting, with the prompt adding details to it. For a place described in words, use the "Keep the moves, change everything else" card (LTX 2.5 IC-LoRA, pose control); to keep the video's own place, use "Replace a person in a video" (SCAIL-2, Wan 2.1). The Motion prompt briefly says what the person in the video is doing (e.g. "a man doing an energetic street dance"). Keep the framing similar in both inputs (full body with full body, close-up with close-up) — a framing mismatch is the #1 cause of bad results. Only the first 81 frames of the video are used by default (about 3 s); both inputs are center-cropped to width × height (portrait 480×848 by default — swap the numbers for a landscape clip). Bigger sizes and more frames take longer.

Prompting: [Wan Animate 2 in ComfyUI](https://docs.comfy.org/tutorials/video/wan/wan-animate-2)

  - `resizeimagemasknode_resize_type_height_261_243` Height — 256…1280, step 16; default 848

### `video_edit_ltx2_5_iclora_pose_control`

**Keep the moves, change everything else** · model: **LTX 2.5 IC-LoRA — video to video (pose control + audio)** · makes **video**

Upload a video of someone moving and describe a new character and place; only the body movements carry over, everything else is new, with a new soundtrack. Pick it for dance and character animation.

> Make a new character perform the movements of the people in your video. Upload a source video with people in it (and, optionally, a start image): the body, hand and face poses of every frame are detected (DWPose) and drawn as a stick-figure guide, so LTX 2.5 generates a new video in which the characters move like the original — while their look, the setting and the lighting come from your prompt and start image. A freshly generated soundtrack is added (the original audio is not kept). Only the poses carry over — not the background, clothes or camera look — so this gives far more freedom than the depth or canny versions. The source needs clearly visible people; a clip with nobody in it gives the model no guide at all. The start image becomes the opening frame; a still of your new character in the first frame's pose works best. Untick "Use a start image" to let the prompt alone set the look — then no image is needed. "Enhance prompt with AI" lets a small Gemma model rewrite your prompt into a fuller description first. Lower "Control strength" to let the movements drift further from the source. Only the start of your clip is used ("Clip length used", default 5 s), at its own frame rate and aspect ratio. The video is rendered in two passes, a fast 8-step pass at the working resolution and then a 2× upscale pass, so a working resolution of 512 gives a 1024p result. Clip length and resolution drive the time.

### `video_edit_minimax_h3_fun_controlnet_canny`

**Redraw a video over its outlines** · model: **MiniMax H3 ControlNet (canny) — restyle a video from its outlines + audio** · makes **video**

Upload a clip and describe a new look; every outline of the original — clothing patterns, buildings, edges — is followed exactly, while colours, materials and sound are all new.

> Upload a video and describe a new look. The clip is turned into an edge map (Canny) and MiniMax H3 generates a brand-new video that follows those outlines — new characters, materials, setting and lighting — with a matching audio track made from your prompt. The original colours and sound are not kept. Describe the scene, what happens over time, the camera and the sounds (the default prompt shows the structure: the new look in prose, then the sound and the music on their own lines). "Control strength" sets how tightly the result sticks to the edges. The two edge thresholds decide how much detail is traced: lower keeps faint edges (more detail, but grainy footage gets noisy and flickers), higher keeps only strong contours. Only the first seconds of your clip are used ("Duration", default 5 s), and the video is centre-cropped to the aspect ratio you pick, so choose the one closest to your clip. The result is always 24 frames a second and follows your clip frame by frame, so a 30 fps clip (what most phones record) comes out about 25% slower: export it at 24 fps first if the timing matters. Time grows with duration and size; the default 20-step render takes a few minutes, "Fast mode" (4-step turbo LoRA) is several times faster at some cost in quality.

Prompting: [MiniMax H3 Fun-ControlNet in ComfyUI](https://docs.comfy.org/tutorials/video/minimax/minimax-h3-fun-controlnet) · [MiniMax H3 prompt guide (ComfyUI) — what works and what does not](https://docs.comfy.org/tutorials/video/minimax/minimax-h3-prompt-guide) · [MiniMax H3 reference-mode prompt guide — MiniMax](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3/blob/main/docs/VIDEO_PROMPT_WRITING_GUIDE_ref_en.md)

  - `resolutionselector_aspect_ratio_115` Aspect ratio (pick the one closest to your video) — one of: 1:1 (Square), 2:3 (Portrait Photo), 3:2 (Photo), 3:4 (Portrait Standard), 4:3 (Standard), 9:16 (Portrait Widescreen), 16:9 (Widescreen), 21:9 (Ultrawide); default 16:9 (Widescreen)
  - `resolutionselector_megapixels_115` Size in megapixels (0.4 = 864x480 at 16:9, 1.0 = 1376x768) — 0.2…1, step 0.1; default 0.4
  - `primitivefloat_value_132` Duration (seconds, 2-15) — 2…15, step 1; default 5
  - `minimaxh3funcontrolnetapply_strength_172` Control strength (1 = follow the video closely, lower = looser) — 0…2, step 0.05; default 1
  - `canny_low_threshold_718` Edge threshold - low (lower keeps fainter edges) — 0.01…0.99, step 0.01; default 0.4
  - `canny_high_threshold_718` Edge threshold - high (higher keeps only strong contours) — 0.01…0.99, step 0.01; default 0.8

### `video_edit_minimax_h3_loop_restyle`

**Repaint a loop, keep it seamless** · model: **MiniMax H3 — restyle a seamless loop (ControlNet) with sound** · makes **video** · experimental

Upload a video that already loops — a simple 3D or depth animation works best — and describe a new look; the motion is kept, everything is repainted with new sound, and it still loops.

> Restyle a video that ALREADY loops seamlessly — a Blender render, a depth pass, an edge pass — with MiniMax H3. Your loop fixes the geometry and timing, H3 paints the look and invents a soundtrack, and the result loops just as cleanly. The author finds this gives the cleanest joints, and it is the way to get camera travel (tunnels, corridors) that a text prompt struggles with. The upload must loop by itself: its frame after the last must be its first. Its frame rate is read from the file. The loop is fitted to the chosen length by repeating it a whole number of times ("Times the control loop plays", 0 = closest to its own speed) and resampling, which blends neighbouring frames; for an exact fit render the control at 24 fps with a cycle that divides the loop (a 34-frame cycle fits 107 frames 3 times). The Fun ControlNet is a union model: a depth or edge render works best. Prompt the geometry the control shows first, then the look. 8 steps with the turbo LoRA v1.0, as in the author's example; clean-sound mode is off because it cannot be combined with the ControlNet.

Prompting: [MiniMax H3 Loop — prompting guide](https://github.com/pxl-pshr/ComfyUI-MiniMaxH3-Loop/blob/main/PROMPTING.md) · [MiniMax H3 Loop — the node pack](https://github.com/pxl-pshr/ComfyUI-MiniMaxH3-Loop)
Tip: Describe a state that keeps going, not a sequence of events: locked-off camera, one subject doing one cyclic thing, steady light and sound. Ask: if this played twice in a row, would the joint show?

Columns: `prompt` (Prompt — describe the geometry the control shows, then the look) · `seed` · `video` Control loop — a video that already loops seamlessly (depth, edges or a rough render) (video, required)

Settings (a column named by the key; empty keeps the default):
  - `strength_33` Control strength — how closely the result follows the control loop — 0…2, step 0.05; default 1
  - `length_40` Loop length in frames (107 = 4.25 s, 158 = 6.4 s, 209 = 8.5 s, 260 = 10.6 s, 311 = 12.75 s) — longer takes pr… — one of: 107, 158, 209, 260, 311; default 107
  - `cycles_32` Times the control loop plays in the result (0 = keep it closest to its own speed) — 0…32, step 1; default 0
  - `width_9` Width (px) — 512…1344, step 32; default 1024
  - `height_9` Height (px) — 512…1344, step 32; default 576
  - `multiplier_23` Smoothing — frame interpolation across the whole loop: 2 = 48 fps, 3 = 72 fps, 4 = 96 fps — one of: 2, 3, 4; default 2

### `video_edit_ltx2_3_3dreal_vid2vid`

**Turn a rough 3D render photoreal** · model: **LTX 2.3 3DReal — rough 3D render to photoreal (render-guided + audio)** · makes **video**

Upload a rough grey 3D animation plus one finished-looking picture of its first frame; it turns the animation into realistic footage with the same camera move, and adds sound. Pick it to preview a 3D scene as if it had been filmed.

> Turn a rough 3D render into a photorealistic clip. Upload a rough 3D render as the source video and a reference image that sets the look; the render itself is the control the 3DREAL IC-LoRA reads (as in fal's own workflow for it), and the clip comes back photoreal with a matching audio track — keeping the render's motion, camera and layout, at the render's own frame rate. The graph adds the trigger word 3DREAL in front of the prompt, on both the typed and the AI-written path. The source is sliced to ~5 s. (Until 2026-11-04 this card fed a MoGe depth map of the render instead, and played a 30 fps render at 25 fps.) Two prompt boxes: with "Enhance prompt with AI" OFF, the "Prompt (used as-is)" box drives generation. With it ON, the "Prompt (AI-enhanced)" box is rewritten by an in-graph LLM using your reference image. The inactive box is greyed out.

Prompting: [LTX IC-LoRA guide — Lightricks](https://docs.ltx.io/open-source-model/usage-guides/ic-lo-ra) · [LTX-2.3 prompt guide — Lightricks blog](https://ltx.io/blog/ltx-2-3-prompt-guide) · [3DREAL LoRA (fal) — trigger word and settings](https://huggingface.co/fal/LTX-2.3-3DREAL-LoRA)
Tip: The trigger word 3DREAL is added for you: describe the photoreal look you want — materials, lighting, lens, atmosphere — and the sound; the layout and motion come from your render.

Columns: `prompt` (Prompt (AI-enhanced)) · `seed` · `image` Reference image (look) (image, required) · `video` Source video (rough 3D render) (video, required)

Settings (a column named by the key; empty keeps the default):
  - `primitiveboolean_value_129_212` Enhance prompt with AI — yes / no; default false
  - `comfyswitchnode_on_false_129_211` Prompt (used as-is); default Make it photorealistic. A photorealistic, cinematic renderi…
  - `primitiveint_value_129_113` Width; default 1280
  - `primitiveint_value_129_98` Height; default 704
  - `video_slice_duration_692` Source clip length (seconds) — 1…10, step 1; default 5
